subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` defaults continue to override later global/agent `tools.exec` config, or should operator config changes invalidate or override stored session exec fields?
rationale: Current code, docs, and tests treat `/exec` as persistent session state, but the report shows that persistence can weaken later operator security policy; automation cannot choose that security/product boundary safely.

options.title: Make operator config the security floor
options.body: Stored session `/exec` values would no longer be able to keep a less restrictive policy after global or agent config is tightened, with migration/reset coverage for existing entries.

options.title: Keep documented session precedence
options.body: Maintain current behavior and add clearer operator reset/doctor guidance for clearing stale session exec defaults when policy changes.

options.title: Add explicit reset/version semantics
options.body: Track exec-policy version or add a targeted reset path so config changes can clear only stale exec overrides without removing all `/exec` persistence.

recommendation.title: Make operator config the security floor
recommendation.body: Stored session `/exec` values would no longer be able to keep a less restrictive policy after global or agent config is tightened, with migration/reset coverage for existing entries.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history links steipete to the original `/exec` session override contract and the current precedence tests.
